answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, foreclosing negotiate_terms as a viable path to meet the mandated 18% cost cut. The primary contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew, forcing a decision now rather than deferral, especially with the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer—deferring risks a supply gap unlike the prior non-critical deferral case (memory_c5). The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate outright, and memory_c2 suggests prior onboarding with them was quick and invoicing reliable, but that record needs verification given the current zero-buffer operating condition, since a botched cutover would directly increase delivery risk. Memory_c1 is checked as the counterfactual baseline (incumbent stability) to confirm what would be lost by switching. Given the no-buffer constraint, I intend a small guarded test/parallel qualification run with the low-cost vendor rather than a full cutover, to validate delivery performance before committing full primary volume—this balances the cost mandate against the risk-increase constraint. This is the one sourcing decision capacity allows this cycle; add_second_source and full switch are deferred pending results of this guarded test.
